title: Broaden the Vision: Geo-Diverse Visual Commonsense Reasoning
findings: Vision-and-language models (VisualBERT, ViLBERT) trained on primarily Western data show a significant performance drop when evaluated on visual commonsense reasoning tasks involving religious scenarios from non-Western regions. The performance gap for scenarios categorized under 'religion' was approximately 12.12% (58.33% accuracy for Western regions vs. 46.21% for other regions), indicating a failure to generalize cultural and religious commonsense.

measurement_description: The benchmark (GD-VCR) measures the ability of vision-and-language models to perform commonsense reasoning on visual scenes depicting geo-diverse cultural scenarios, including religious activities, to test for geographical bias.
